artists.biography:
The group was formed by guitarist, singer and chief songwriter Bill Fisher and keyboardist Michael Wetherburn over a mutual love of musical theatre and Queen. The group members had previously played in various bands in and around Nottingham, and a number of early songs by the group had been written years before while in other bands. Fisher was more interested in progressive pop rather than progressive rock, and wanted the band to be primarily about good songwriting over pointless technical ability. His influences include The Beatles, Kate Bush, David Bowie and Peter Gabriel, The instrumentation makes prominent use of the Hammond organ.

The band is signed to Bilocation Records. They have also covered Pink Floyd's "The Trial" on Magnetic Eye Records' tribute album The Wall Redux. Fisher has described the group as a "twofold entity: a new religious movement…and a 7-piece supergroup".

In 2017, the group released "Evil in your Eye" from their first album Is Satan Real? on 21 August to coincide with the solar eclipse on the same day.
Bill Fisher - guitar, vocals
Joanne Joyce - vocals
Caroline Cawley - vocals
Michael Wetherburn - keyboards, vocals
Amy Nicholson - cello, vocals
Sam Lloyd - bass
Loz Stone - drums

perplexity.description:
There Is No Time, released in 2022 on Septaphonic Records, is the fourth studio album by British rock band Church of the Cosmic Skull. The album continues the band's blend of classic rock influences with a modern psychedelic and progressive touch, featuring rich harmonies, melodic guitar work, and layered vocals that have become their signature style. It explores themes of cosmic spirituality and human connection, maintaining the band's characteristic optimistic and communal ethos.

Musically, There Is No Time introduces some subtle shifts in the band's sound, incorporating new textures and slightly more varied arrangements while staying true to their melodic rock foundation. Critics have noted the album's strong group vocals and moments of engaging songwriting, though some reviews suggest it does not surpass the impact of their earlier work, such as the standout track "Do You Believe in Magic." Overall, the album holds a solid place in Church of the Cosmic Skull's discography as a continuation of their evolving sound and thematic focus, receiving a generally positive but mixed critical reception.
